spot.html_text: Consider, again, a possible world ⟦M⟧ , in which there are two qualitatively indiscernible globes; call them Castor and Pollux. Being indiscernible, they have of course the same duration; in ⟦M⟧ both of them have always existed and always will exist. But it seems perfectly possible, logically and metaphysically, that either or both of them cease to exist. Let ⟦M⟧ , then, be a possible world just like ⟦M⟧ up to a certain time ⟦M⟧ at which in ⟦M⟧ Castor ceases to exist while Pollux goes on forever
